novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism-level phenomenon—“multilingual LLM builds a shared, language-agnostic agent/patient representation” but “lazily applies its DOMINANT language's word-order-first cue hierarchy,” causing cross-lingual role reversals—rather than merely a new setting or a renamed measurement. The closest prior work found was “Do Language Models Know Who Did What to Whom?” (2025), which studies thematic-role information and attention heads in largely monolingual models, alongside “How Do Multilingual Language Models Remember Facts?” (2024), which uses multilingual activation patching but concerns factual recall rather than role-cue arbitration; searches included “multilingual LLM thematic role assignment word order case marking,” “LLM cue hierarchy agent patient multilingual,” “mechanistic interpretability thematic roles attention heads,” and “cross-lingual activation patching thematic roles.” The step from these works and the human Competition-Model literature to the proposed claim requires a new core relationship—dominant-language cue-hierarchy import under conflicting cues—although the causal patching and steering components use established interpretability techniques, supporting high but not paradigm-level novelty.
